brief: Goldman's Miller frames Thursday's reversal as a resumption of AI panic after Wednesday's post-midterm relief: the firm's vol panic index hit 9.57/10 and Cboe logged record put volume. Prime data shows de-grossing in eight of the last nine sessions, pushing fundamental long/short net leverage to its lowest since May 2025; as positioning nears washout levels, Goldman likes buying the rebound in Hyperscalers for their AI-monetization potential. Asia AI hedging rose alongside the US unwind, but China Domestic AI decoupled on policy support and national-team buying, and Goldman re-engages that trade on compressed valuations. Separately, the defensive rotation that made sense in October has pushed US and European Staples valuations beyond what earnings justify, so Goldman recommends shorting US Staples and a dual binary on Staples and rates falling. Receding Iran war-risk (Brent sub-$100, European gas down 17% on the week) is deflating the Hormuz Bottleneck trade, which Goldman sees as vulnerable given consensus expects declining EPS, recommending limited-loss puts. Credit spreads stayed resilient despite the equity selloff, but Goldman's credit desk expects that to break in a risk-off scenario and recommends shorting IG 30Y versus long S&P futures.
